sections.overview: Myxobolus cerebralis is a microscopic freshwater parasite that causes whirling disease in salmon and trout and other salmonids.
sections.identification: Its microscopic spore stages are not recognizable by ordinary visual inspection, so diagnosis depends on laboratory examination of fish or parasite material.
sections.habitat: It occurs in freshwater systems where susceptible salmonid fish and the oligochaete worm Tubifex tubifex overlap.
sections.diet: It is a parasite rather than a free-living feeder, developing in the tissues of its fish and worm hosts.
sections.behavior: Infected young salmonids may show abnormal circling, darkened tails or skeletal deformities, though infection can occur without visible signs.
sections.reproduction: Its two-host cycle alternates between spores developing in salmonid cartilage and an infective stage released by Tubifex worms into the water.
sections.ecology: The parasite can damage cartilage and impair fish movement, and the resulting disease may affect wild salmonid populations as well as fish farms.
sections.conservation: No conservation status is applicable to the parasite in the sources consulted; its importance is as a pathogen whose spread threatens susceptible fish populations.
